With roughly 4,683 residents age 65 and older, Clarke County is 44th among 67 Alabama counties for older residents. That group is 21.0% of its population, compared with 18.3% across Alabama. Another 1,618 residents are age 60 to 64 and will reach Medicare eligibility within about five years (see our turning 65 guide). Among residents 65 and older, 54% are 65 to 74, 34% are 75 to 84 and 12% are 85 or older (Census 2023 estimates). CMS data show 69.3% of Clarke County residents with Medicare chose Medicare Advantage, which is higher than the 61.5% average across Alabama. What most people do in a county is less important than what fits you. We weigh Medicare Advantage against Original Medicare with Medigap using your doctors, your drugs and your budget.

Who has Medicare in Clarke County

Clarke County is a rural county; the U.S. Department of Agriculture describes it as: urban population of fewer than 5,000, not adjacent to a metro area. Rural counties tend to have fewer local hospitals and doctors, so a plan’s network and the distance to care matter a great deal.

CMS counts 6,662 Medicare beneficiaries in Clarke County (2023). Their average age is 72, about the same as the Alabama average of 72. About 18% are “dual eligible,” meaning they have both Medicare and Medicaid, higher than the state figure of 14%. Where many people have both, special plans for dual-eligible members can matter; see our Medicaid and dual eligible guide, since availability varies by plan and area.

Among people in Original Medicare in Clarke County, CMS reported about 753 emergency room visits and 237 inpatient hospital stays per 1,000 beneficiaries in 2023, which is higher than the state average for emergency visits (600) and close to it for hospital stays (247). About 13% received home health care. These figures describe how people use care under Original Medicare; they do not show what any plan covers or costs.

Sources: CMS Medicare Geographic Variation, 2023; USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Codes, 2023.

Insurers choose which counties to serve each year, which means the Medicare Advantage and Part D plans you can pick in Clarke County can be different from the ones offered next door. We are not based in Clarke County; we help Clarke County residents by phone or video call.

Hospitals located in Clarke County

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) lists these hospitals in Clarke County:

  • Grove Hill Memorial Hospital — Grove Hill (acute care; government-owned; emergency services)
  • Jackson Medical Center — Jackson (acute care; for-profit; emergency services)

Network rules, not geography, decide whether a plan covers a hospital. We look up the hospitals and doctors you use and check them against each plan before you enroll. Ratings are CMS Care Compare overall hospital star ratings; they describe the hospital, not whether a plan covers it. Source: CMS Hospital General Information.

Common questions

Clarke County Medicare FAQ

Can I get help with Medicare in Clarke County by phone?
Yes. We are an independent agency licensed in Alabama, and we help Clarke County residents by phone or video call, so you can compare plans from home. There is no pressure to enroll.
Will my Clarke County doctors and hospitals be covered?
On a Medicare Advantage plan it depends on that plan’s network, so before you enroll we check whether your doctors and the hospitals you use, such as Grove Hill Memorial Hospital, Jackson Medical Center, are in network. With a Medicare Supplement (Medigap) plan you can see any doctor who accepts Medicare.
How many people in Clarke County have Medicare Advantage?
CMS reported 4,403 people enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan out of 6,350 people with Medicare in Clarke County in September 2026, or 69.3%. The Alabama average was 61.5%.
Do you charge Clarke County residents for help?
No. You pay nothing to work with us. Carriers compensate us, and the price of your plan is the same as if you enrolled directly.
When can I enroll or change plans?
You can enroll during your Initial Enrollment Period around your 65th birthday, during the Annual Enrollment Period from October 15 to December 7, or during a Special Enrollment Period if you have a qualifying event such as moving into or within the county.
